The amount of your premium payments that go into the account may be less than you paid because fees were taken out of the payments.
The money in the account gets invested in a selection of investment options—typically mutual funds— that you can choose.
question: How are premiums handled in variable life insurance, and what investment options are used?
answer: Premiums go into an account, but fees may be deducted first, so the full amount you pay may not be invested. The money in the account is invested in options you choose, typically mutual funds. The policy’s cash value can vary partly with how those investments perform.
